reviews.comment: Diagnosis for diagnosis at the same grain. CLM-PE-DIAGNOSIS-01 names sudden dyspnea, pleuritic pain, haemoptysis, hypoxemia and VTE risk factors as the features that raise pretest probability, so all three stated discriminators are the direct negation of claim-listed features, and CLM-ACS-DIAGNOSIS-01 supplies the positive counterpart (regional ST depression or T-wave inversion). The seed's 'troponin also rises in PE' framing is not itself in the packet, but it carries only the temptation, not the defeat, and the defeat is fully cited. Defeated by positive exertional/ECG features, not by a written-in exclusion.

CLM-AORTIC-DISSECTION-01 states abrupt severe pain maximal at onset with possible pulse or blood-pressure differences, which is exactly the onset-profile discriminator the seed relies on, so the load-bearing defeat is cited and is a positive history feature (crescendo exertional onset) rather than an exclusion clause. The seed's added assertion that dissection must be settled 'before antithrombotic treatment' is not in the cited claim, but it only decorates the plausibility rationale and nothing in the discrimination rests on it. A genuinely competitive near miss in any severe acute chest pain stem.

This is the cleanest seed in the target: CLM-PERICARDITIS-01 states the sharp, pleuritic, positional pain and the widespread-rather-than-territorial ST elevation or PR depression pattern, and CLM-ACS-DIAGNOSIS-01 states that new regional ST depression or T-wave inversion supports NSTE-ACS, so both discriminators are literally in the cited text. The ECG discriminator is a positive finding on the tracing the stem must show anyway. Strongly competitive for any candidate who reads the tracing as merely abnormal.

CLM-GERD-01 does support the discrimination (heartburn/regurgitation as the typical presentation, cardiac evaluation before GERD testing), so check 6 is not the problem. The problem is check 4: this target's key is NSTE-ACS, which by CLM-ACS-DIAGNOSIS-01 requires an ischemic context with acute myocardial injury, so the stem will necessarily carry a rising troponin and a dynamic or ischaemic tracing. Against those printed findings reflux is discardable on sight and attracts no partially knowledgeable candidate; the seed's own discriminator ('the troponin is rising and the tracing is changing') concedes this. It is a filler option, not a competitive near miss.

CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 names hypotension with elevated JVP and clear lungs as the right-ventricular signature and explicitly says to avoid preload-reducing nitrates, with the ACC/AHA locator adding avoidance in suspected RV infarction or SBP under 90. Both the temptation (nitrate as the reflex ischaemic action) and the defeat are carried by the same cited claim, and the defeat rests on findings the vignette must already report. Action for action at the same grain, and a classic candidate error.

The same claim explicitly instructs avoidance of diuretics in this physiology and pairs the raised JVP with clear lung fields, so the very finding that tempts the candidate is the one the claim uses to defeat the diuretic. Clear lungs and hypotension are natural elements of the right-ventricular triad rather than a clause inserted to switch this option off. Genuinely selectable by a candidate who reads a raised JVP as congestion.

CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 states directly that beta blockade must not be initiated or escalated during a low-output state or cardiogenic-shock risk and should be reassessed after stabilization, which supports both the recall-the-bundle temptation and the defeat. The specific numbers the seed quotes (84/56 mmHg, 58 beats/min) are stem detail, not claimed thresholds, and the claim's 'low-output state' covers them. Downgraded to ACCEPTABLE rather than STRONG because a printed hypotension plus bradycardia makes intravenous metoprolol eliminable by a wider band of candidates than the nitrate or diuretic options.

CLM-ACS-AMI-CARDIOGENIC-SHOCK-01 defines AMI cardiogenic shock as persistent hypotension or vasopressor requirement WITH end-organ hypoperfusion, so the seed's discriminator (warm peripheries, alert, maintained urine output) is the claim's own missing definitional element, and CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 supplies the preload-first sequence. Perfusion status is a natural part of assessing any hypotensive infarct patient, so no exclusion clause is required. Strongly competitive for anyone who equates a low blood pressure with shock.

I checked the number: CLM-ACS-PHARMACOINVASIVE-01 carries the 120-minute first-medical-contact-to-device threshold explicitly, so the seed's four-hour estimate sits unambiguously on the fibrinolysis side of a cited threshold. CLM-ACS-FIBRINOLYSIS-CONTRA-PPCI-01 independently supports the stated condition under which transfer for primary PCI would instead be correct. The strongest competitor in this target, since preference for primary PCI is exactly what candidates over-generalize.

CLM-ACS-PHARMACOINVASIVE-01 states routine rapid transfer AFTER fibrinolysis with angiography within 24 hours if reperfusion succeeds, which is precisely what makes failure-contingent transfer wrong, so the claim itself carries the discrimination rather than a stem clause. It matches the key on drug and timing and differs only on transfer policy, which is the single most commonly omitted element of the pharmacoinvasive strategy. Same reperfusion-action category and grain as the compound key.

The 24-hour window the discriminator depends on is stated verbatim in CLM-ACS-PHARMACOINVASIVE-01 ('angiography within 24 hours if reperfusion succeeds'), so the three-to-five-day alternative is defeated by the cited interval and not by anything written into the stem. It shares the drug, the timing of lysis and the eventual angiography with the key and differs only on the interval, which is a real point of candidate confusion. Same action category and grain.

Check 4 fails. A doubly conditional option ('transfer, and lyse en route if the flight is delayed') is dominated in both directions: a candidate who favours primary PCI picks the clean transfer option, and a candidate who knows the 120-minute rule picks the key, so almost nobody selects the hedge, and hedged compound options read as constructed. I also note a citation defect the author should fix even though it did not decide the verdict: CLM-ACS-REPERFUSION-NO-DELAY-01 is about not delaying reperfusion for biomarkers or additional diagnostic testing, not about contingent transfer logistics, so it does not say what the seed uses it to say; only CLM-ACS-PHARMACOINVASIVE-01 actually carries the defeat. The stated 'conditions under which the competitor would be correct' also describes no recognised strategy.

CLM-ACS-NSTE-HIGH-RISK-DISPOSITION-01 names outpatient stress testing by name as reserved for lower-risk or diagnostically uncertain presentations, and states that a troponin rise or fall with dynamic ST or T changes is high risk EVEN IF symptoms resolve, which is exactly the trap this seed sets. The defeat therefore rests on positive test findings the stem must report, not on an exclusion clause. Disposition for disposition at the same grain.

The cited claim explicitly reserves 'observation without an invasive plan' for lower-risk or diagnostically uncertain presentations, so the wording of the competitor maps onto a phrase in the claim text and the discrimination is carried by evidence rather than by inference. It is the cautious middle course that a candidate unwilling to discharge but unaware of the early-invasive requirement will pick, so it is genuinely competitive. Defeated by the confirmed high-risk criteria already in the stem.

Discharge with outpatient follow-up is named in CLM-ACS-NSTE-HIGH-RISK-DISPOSITION-01 as reserved for lower-risk presentations, so the defeat is cited, and rapid-access chest pain clinics are a real Canadian ambulatory pathway, so the context check holds. Marked ACCEPTABLE rather than STRONG because it is defeated by exactly the same reasoning as SEED-G2-MED-T04-DISCHARGE-STRESS and adds only a different follow-up label; it is the weaker of the two go-home options and the two should not appear in the same item.

The cited claim requires admission plus an EARLY INPATIENT INVASIVE strategy for confirmed high-risk NSTE-ACS, and its ACC/AHA locator states that noninvasive testing is for lower-risk patients, so the seed's discriminator is supported at the exact point of difference. This is the best competitor in the target because it concedes the admission half of the key and fails only on strategy, which is where partial knowledge actually stops. No exclusion clause needed.

CLM-R2-PHELO-LEAD-TIME ties the bias specifically to evaluating a programme by survival time AFTER DIAGNOSIS, so a result in which survival from diagnosis does not differ positively defeats it, and CLM-R2-PHELO-HEALTHY-VOLUNTEER entails that self-selected screenees are healthier and therefore do better on outcomes generally, which is what a difference in mortality from causes screening cannot affect would show. Named bias for named bias, same closed family, same grain. It is the reflex answer to any favourable screening result, so it is maximally competitive against a healthy-screenee key.

Edit for edit on the same document at the same grain. CLM-R4-PHELO-CONSENT-CRITERION grounds voluntariness and consent as genuine autonomy content, so the temptation is evidence-backed, while CLM-R2-PHELO-ACCEPTABILITY states that autonomy may be compromised BY THE WAY INFORMATION IS GIVEN, which is what makes an information-quality edit beat a voluntariness statement, and CLM-R4-PHELO-ABSOLUTE identifies the uninterpretable relative figure as the specific defect. The defeat therefore comes from the letter's stated defect rather than an exclusion clause. One drafting condition: the item must state that defect explicitly, or the two edits become co-defensible.

Check 6 fails. The load-bearing discriminator is a legal proposition, that certification is engaged only when a needed admission is declined, and neither cited claim contains it: CLM-R2-PSY-INPATIENT says only that inpatient treatment is often warranted for high-risk patients, and CLM-R2-PSY-SAFETY-PLAN is about individualized care, therapeutic risk management, means removal and professional contacts. Nothing in the packet mentions involuntary admission, capacity, refusal, or provincial mental health legislation, so the entire discrimination rests on uncited general knowledge, and a jurisdictional legal threshold is exactly the kind of assertion that must be evidenced before an item is written. The competitor is otherwise well formed and could be re-submitted once a certification-criteria claim is admitted.

CLM-R2-PSY-SAFETY-PLAN explicitly includes removing lethal means and identifying professional contacts, which is precisely what makes the community package tempting, and CLM-R2-PSY-INPATIENT names suicidal ideation WITH INTENT TO ACT as the high-risk state for which inpatient treatment is warranted, which defeats it. The decisive discriminator, stated intent to act tonight, is a positive clinical feature of the presentation rather than a clause written to switch the option off. Disposition for disposition at the same grain, and least-restrictive-option reasoning makes it strongly selectable.

Check 6 fails on both halves. I read the two stone claims: CLM-R4-SURG-STONE-IMAGING is only about ultrasound with KUB versus low-dose CT as the imaging pathway, and CLM-R4-SURG-STONE-CONSERVATIVE is only about spontaneous passage of stones under 5 mm; neither states a single clinical feature of ureteral colic, so 'radiating from flank to groin', 'urinalysis shows no blood' and 'fever, rebound and leukocytosis are not features of uncomplicated colic' are all uncited general knowledge. Neither claim even places a ureteral stone in the right-lower-quadrant differential, and the packet's own differential claims (CLM-R4-SURG-FEMALE-DDX, CLM-R4-SURG-NORMAL-APPENDIX) do not list it, so the plausibility side is unsupported too. CLM-R4-SURG-ALVARADO-COMPONENTS supplies only the appendicitis-side score components and discriminates nothing about the stone; this is the same defect for which this competitor concept was rejected in the R4 review, and adding the Alvarado citation does not repair it.

CLM-R2-PSY-ECT names severe suicide risk and physical deterioration as its qualifying examples, and the seed's two discriminators negate exactly those two named examples, so the defeat is carried by the claim's own wording and by findings (eating and drinking, no suicidal intent) that any depression assessment reports anyway. Treatment plan for treatment plan at the same grain, and it is highly selectable by a candidate who maps severity onto one escalating ladder. I withhold STRONG because the claim reads 'in the most severe episodes AND/OR in life-threatening situations': the defeat holds only if the 'for example' list is taken to operationalize the severity limb as well, and a severe episode with psychotic features sits at that end. The item must therefore print the eating/drinking and no-suicidal-intent findings so the qualifier is visibly unmet, or ECT becomes a second defensible answer.

CLM-R2-PSY-FIRST-LINE establishes that a first-line antidepressant is an evidence-supported initial agent, which is exactly the temptation, and CLM-R2-PSY-ANTIPSYCHOTIC states verbatim that for severe major depressive episodes WITH PSYCHOTIC SYMPTOMS the combination of an antidepressant and an atypical antipsychotic is recommended, which is exactly the defeat. The discrimination therefore turns on the psychotic features the stem must already report, a positive finding rather than a clause written to switch the option off. Same treatment-plan category and grain as the key, containing half of it, so it is the commonest incomplete answer and a genuinely competitive near miss.
